validated_results.title: Distribution of polyunsaturated fatty acids including conjugated linoleic acids in total and subcellular fractions from healthy and cancerous parts of human kidneys.
validated_results.reason: This study compares fatty acid composition of subcellular fractions in healthy versus cancerous kidney tissue from the same patients, providing tumor-tissue/mechanistic data without any estimate of risk of developing kidney cancer.

validated_results.title: Distribution of polyunsaturated fatty acids including conjugated linoleic acids in total and subcellular fractions from healthy and cancerous parts of human kidneys.
validated_results.reason: PUFA contents were measured in resected renal cell carcinoma versus adjacent healthy tissue, a tumor-tissue metabolic comparison with no incidence estimate for renal cell carcinoma.

validated_results.title: Major dietary patterns and risk of renal cell carcinoma in a prospective cohort of Swedish women.
validated_results.reason: Alcohol appears only inside the multi-item "Drinker" dietary pattern (wine, hard liquor, beer, snacks) derived by factor analysis, with no alcohol-specific risk estimate reported.

validated_results.title: Major dietary patterns and risk of renal cell carcinoma in a prospective cohort of Swedish women.
validated_results.reason: High-fat dairy products are only a component of the composite "Western" dietary pattern score, and no dairy-specific estimate for renal cell carcinoma is provided.

validated_results.title: Major dietary patterns and risk of renal cell carcinoma in a prospective cohort of Swedish women.
validated_results.reason: Processed meat is only one item loading on the composite "Western" dietary pattern, with no separable processed-meat risk estimate.

validated_results.title: Major dietary patterns and risk of renal cell carcinoma in a prospective cohort of Swedish women.
validated_results.reason: Tomato is included only as a constituent of the composite "Healthy" dietary pattern, and no tomato-specific estimate for renal cell carcinoma is reported.

validated_results.title: Major dietary patterns and risk of renal cell carcinoma in a prospective cohort of Swedish women.
validated_results.reason: Whole grains contribute only to the composite "Healthy" dietary pattern score, so no whole-grain-specific renal cell carcinoma estimate can be separated.

validated_results.title: Association of genetic polymorphism of glutathione S-transferase M1, T1, P1 and susceptibility to bladder cancer.
validated_results.reason: The study evaluates GSTM1, GSTT1 and GSTP1 genotype polymorphisms as bladder cancer risk factors and reports no nutritional glutathione exposure estimate.

validated_results.title: Diet and bladder cancer: a case-control study.
validated_results.reason: Hospital-based case-control study in Serbia reporting a multivariable-adjusted odds ratio for egg consumption and newly diagnosed bladder cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: Highest vs lowest tertile of average daily intake
extraction.population: Newly diagnosed bladder cancer patients and sex-, age- and residence-matched controls

cases.excerpt: This study included 130 newly diagnosed bladder cancer patients and the same number of controls matched by sex, age (%+/-%2 years) and type of residence (rural or urban).

effect_size.excerpt: According to this analysis, risk factors for bladder cancer appeared to be consumption of liver (OR=6.60, 95%CI=1.89-23.03), eggs (OR=3.12, 95%CI=1.10-8.80), pork (OR=2.99, 95%CI=1.16-7.72), and pickled vegetable (OR=3.25, 95%CI=1.36-7.71).

confidence_interval.excerpt: According to this analysis, risk factors for bladder cancer appeared to be consumption of liver (OR=6.60, 95%CI=1.89-23.03), eggs (OR=3.12, 95%CI=1.10-8.80), pork (OR=2.99, 95%CI=1.16-7.72), and pickled vegetable (OR=3.25, 95%CI=1.36-7.71).

comparison.excerpt: Initial case-control comparisons were based on tertiles of average daily intake of control group. The odds ratios (ORs) were computed for each tertile, with the lowest tertile defined as the referent category.
